why: Cutting the edge above node v splits the tree into v's subtree and everything else, so the difference is |total - 2 * flow(v)|. Subtree flows come from one bottom-up pass, and the answer is the minimum over all non-root v.
hints: When you cut the edge between v and its parent, what are the two parts?
One part is v's subtree with flow S(v); the other has total - S(v). The difference is |total - 2 * S(v)|.
parent[i] < i, so loop i from n-1 down to 1 adding S(i) into S(parent[i]): no recursion needed. Take the min over i >= 1. O(n).
pitfalls: The root has no edge above it; only nodes 1..n-1 are candidate cuts.
Flow means subtree sum, not the node's own input.
